title: Shimon ben Gurion
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, at the end of chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.5.11.3), relates that the sages allotted Miriam, daughter of Shimon ben Gurion, five hundred dinars for a basket of perfumes. [Ketubot 66b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.66b.10) relates the incident about Nakdimon ben Gurion’s daughter.[^1][^2]
Hyman adds that he was also called Buni, citing [Taanit 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.20a.4).[^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s [printed notice](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=329) reads “end of chapter 5” (ספ״ה). The supplied transcription has מפ״ה.

In the Yerushalmi and [Heilprin’s notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3435&lang=en), the allowance for Shimon’s daughter is five hundred denars each day. The Bavli gives Nakdimon’s daughter four hundred gold coins for that day.
Taanit identifies Nakdimon as Buni. Hyman compares the accounts of the two daughters.
